title: Judge execution has stopped progressing
slo: No due judge execution remains without progress for ten minutes
summary: Platform-worker SQL snapshot found due queue/recovery/finalization work with no progress for ten minutes, or a running execution with both stale progress and an expired/missing lease. A live lease avoids alerting on legitimate long-running stages. Inspect the execution journal and runtime ownership; do not release leases by age alone.

title: Judge queue oldest wait exceeds twenty minutes
summary: The oldest queued, capacity-waiting or recovering execution has waited over twenty minutes, longer than an exam burst queues. This gauge comes from the platform worker database snapshot and remains available when the judge worker is offline.

title: Judge automatic recovery is blocked
slo: System errors retain an actionable recovery owner
summary: One or more executions need infrastructure or configuration repair before their original-version recovery can continue. Inspect reasonCode and cleanup ownership; do not ask teachers to rejudge infrastructure failures.

title: Legacy system errors lack an immutable execution journal
slo: Every system error has a recoverable original-version record
summary: Some SE submissions have no execution journal, so their original snapshot cannot be assumed. Inventory historical evidence; do not silently recover them using the current problem version.

title: Judge recovery monitoring stopped reporting
slo: Judge recovery database snapshot is refreshed at least every three minutes
summary: The last successful platform-worker SQL snapshot is over three minutes old or absent. Check platform worker, PostgreSQL and OTEL exporter/collector connectivity. Missing monitoring is a fault even when no submission metrics are present.

title: HTTP 5xx error rate above availability SLO
summary: HTTP 5xx error rate has exceeded 1% for 5 minutes — service availability SLO is breached. Page on-call immediately.

title: Node filesystem usage over 80%
summary: A node filesystem has exceeded 80% usage for 10m. A full disk wedges containerd and gets CNPG evicted. Free disk (crictl rmi --prune) or expand the volume before it fills. Requires observability.prometheus.nodeExporter.enabled.

title: Postgres (CloudNativePG) instance not ready
slo: Database availability - all CNPG instances reachable
summary: One or more CloudNativePG Postgres instances failed scrape (not ready) for 2m. Postgres is the single durable store — a down instance means degraded or total outage. Dormant until a CNPG metrics scrape target (job=cnpg-postgres) is wired; see docs/operations/RELIABILITY.md.

title: Postgres dump older than 8 days
slo: Backup freshness - last successful weekly pg_dump < 8 days old
summary: The weekly pg_dump CronJob has not completed successfully in over 8 days (Saturday schedule + margin), or the platform worker cannot read its status. Check the latest postgres-dump Job logs. See docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md.

title: Object mirror older than 26h
slo: Backup freshness - last successful object mirror < 26h old
summary: The daily object-store mirror CronJob has not completed successfully in over 26h, or the platform worker cannot read its status. Check the latest minio-backup Job logs. See docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md.

title: Notification email exhausted delivery retries
slo: No notification email durable work reaches the dead state
summary: An at-least-once notification email exhausted its database-owned retries. Inspect the DurableWork lastError/result and SMTP health. A stable Message-ID helps recipients deduplicate retries but does not provide exactly-once delivery.

title: Judge cleanup requires retry
slo: Judge leases remain held until sandbox termination
summary: Sandbox termination exceeded its cleanup deadline. The execution lease remains held; inspect run ID and Pod UID in worker logs. Verify CRI, shim and cgroup ownership before targeted recovery; do not restart the runtime automatically.

title: Judge TLEs decided by wall clock
slo: Concurrent judging must not turn CPU-bounded runs into time limit exceeded
summary: Several runs hit the wall-clock ceiling while their CPU time stayed under the limit. That is sleeping programs or CPU contention; if it coincides with judge load, lower worker.judge.concurrency (the slot tuner ceiling) and rejudge the affected submissions.
